additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as vomiting, fasting, excessive exercise, or misuse of laxatives/diuretics) aimed at preventing weight gain. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body shape and weight, but individuals typically maintain a body weight within or near the normal range, distinguishing it from anorexia nervosa. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress, interpersonal difficulties, and changes in life structure or mood. It must be differentiated from binge-eating disorder, which lacks regular compensatory behaviors, and from primary mood or anxiety disorders where eating changes are secondary rather than driven by weight/shape concerns.

patient.personality: A gentle, community‑minded retiree who balances practical handiwork with reflective, artistic pursuits and takes quiet pride in staying active and useful to others.
patient.stressor: Following a minor cardiac scare and a stern warning from his doctor about his blood pressure and cholesterol, Daniel became preoccupied with the idea that gaining any weight would threaten his independence and ability to keep working in his garden and volunteering. He began reading diet advice online and in magazines, internalizing strict rules about “good” and “bad” foods that clashed with the communal meals and baked goods that were a big part of his social life at the senior center. When he did allow himself to eat more at family gatherings or potlucks, he would later respond with increasingly rigid attempts to compensate—skipping meals, walking or doing chores far beyond his usual routine, and quietly berating himself for perceived lapses. Over six months, this push‑pull between enjoying food in social settings and then trying to “fix” it afterward left him feeling ashamed and fatigued, and after a volunteer coordinator gently asked why he seemed so worn down and anxious about food at events, he agreed to talk with a mental health professional at the clinic attached to the senior center.
patient.chief_complaint: “Whenever I eat more than I think I should, I feel like I have to overdo it with cutting back or extra activity afterward.”

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Ever since that heart scare, if the scale creeps up even a pound or my belt feels a little tighter, I get this knot in my stomach and start thinking, 'If I don't get this back down right away, I'll end up in a wheelchair and lose my garden and my freedom.'

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: I catch myself judging my whole day by whether my stomach looks flat in the bathroom mirror or if I can still see the veins in my hands, like if I look a bit softer then I'm lazy and letting everyone down at the senior center.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: On days after a big family dinner or a potluck, I’ll often skip breakfast and sometimes even lunch and then force myself to walk extra laps around the block or do chores until I’m worn out, telling myself I have to 'work off' what I ate.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: There have been a few times after I really overdid it at a party that I went to the bathroom and made myself throw up, and I’ve also taken extra stool softeners at night, telling myself it’ll help get the food out faster so it doesn’t turn into weight.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: When I get home from a church supper or a birthday, I replay how I went back for seconds and thirds of the casseroles and desserts, piling my plate higher than most of the others at the table and nibbling nonstop even when I already felt full.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start in on the cookies or the homemade bread at these gatherings, it feels like a switch flips and I just keep reaching for more even while I’m scolding myself in my head and telling myself to stop, but my hand doesn’t listen.
